source.title: The Anatomy of a Truth Direction: Knowledge-Dependent Dimensionality, a Relational Law, and a Convergent Category Geometry in Small Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-model agreement in category-level truth geometry and refines the convergence claim: agreement is positive but incomplete, differs within versus across families, and is sensitive to measurement choices. It also tests and rejects a proposed shared-distillation-lineage explanation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports measurements of category-axis agreement across models, early-layer and embedding controls, and changes under alternate sentence construction and category-selection protocols. These bear on metric/data dependence and partial cross-model convergence. It does not test whether alignment rises with model size or capability, cross-modal image-caption alignment, same-architecture feature convergence across training seeds, representational mapping or stitching, or recurring interpretable features. Other results about truth probing and FFN mechanisms are not included unless they directly measure cross-model category geometry.
record.test_reason: Part III measures how far independently trained LMs from six families agree on the arrangement of per-category truth axes (attenuation-corrected Mantel). That is a new setting and a second-order similarity measure with results on cross-model convergence. It also probes causes: family effect, a distillation-lineage test and instruction tuning. It does not test any scale trend, and the paper is not aimed at the Platonic hypothesis, so T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the per-category truth arrangement is largely shared across families with a measurable family-specific component (they retract a stronger 'identical' claim), and that it is built by the blocks: near zero at an early block, absent at the embeddings. Their pre-registered shared-distillation-lineage hypothesis failed. They treat the earlier K=8 sign instability as a measurement pathology removed by the final protocol. They leave the Gemma-it outlier unexplained and limit scope to models under 4B on CounterFact.
record.recipe_differences: Measures signed cosine arrangements of per-category truth axes and corrected Mantel agreement across language models, rather than testing the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with its original representation-similarity setup. The study does not test model scale or capability as predictors of alignment.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured geometry varies with layer (near-zero early agreement versus positive peak-layer agreement), sentence suffix (global-axis cosine 0.474 while arrangement Mantel correlation is +0.775), category selection and knowledge gate (for OLMo-2-1B reliability 0.586 full versus 0.905 restricted), and sign gauge/category subset in the earlier protocol.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed small scale (≤3B), independently trained LMs of six families share the second-order arrangement of per-category truth axes (corrected mean 0.798). The agreement is near zero at an early block, and the arrangement is absent at the embeddings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model convergence of relational/conceptual geometry exists already at small scale, independent of any scale trend, and is built by the transformer blocks rather than inherited from input lexical structure.

record.problems: All tested models are below four billion parameters and all measurements use CounterFact. No scale or capability trend in cross-model agreement is tested. Cross-family agreement uses attenuation correction that assumes one common factor with independent errors; the authors report that reliability-estimate error propagates into corrected values. Some protocol-dependence results come from an earlier eight-category analysis that the authors say was unstable.
record.rows_left_out: No additional cross-model category-geometry outcomes directly bearing on V6 or V7 were left out. Other reported results concern truth-axis readability, polarity, component interventions, or circuit norms rather than convergence across models.

untested.parts: No test of whether cross-model agreement rises with size or capability. All models are below 4B, and the per-model ranking is not analysed against scale.
The seeds are data-sampling seeds, not training initialisations.
No mapping, stitching or transfer across models is reported.
No recurring neurons, SAE features or circuits across models are measured.
No alternative similarity metrics (CKA, kNN), neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution inputs. Cross-model agreement on the full (unrestricted) category set is not reported.
No plateau test. Shared data or objectives are not directly compared with a common-model-of-reality explanation, apart from the family, lineage and instruction-tuning contrasts.

missing.what: Matched-seed (shared-sentence) inflation of cross-model agreement: +0.035 (SE 0.016) between Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.2-3B. This bears on dependence of measured convergence on the inputs used.

Full per-model mean corrected agreement ranking (Qwen2.5-Coder-3B 0.860 … Gemma-2-2b-it 0.670). The two MoE models sit inside the range. A researcher could use it to check a size trend that the authors don't analyse.

record.verdict_notes: The convergence measure is second-order: a Mantel correlation between signed cosine matrices of per-category truth axes, divided by sqrt of each model's reliability. The reported cross-model figures are corrected values, and raw values are not given in the text. Most V6-linked rows in the record were within-model reliability or stability checks and were relinked to none. Only R11/R12 measure cross-model agreement under alternative choices, and both come from a superseded protocol. The study cites the Platonic hypothesis [17] for the shared-arrangement reading but tests no scale trend.

versions.untested_parts: The study compares cross-model geometry but does not test whether alignment increases with size or capability.
No vision-language model pairs or paired images and captions are studied.
The four seeds are sampling seeds for dictionary bundles, not different training initializations of the same architecture.
The paper describes a held-out transfer matrix but reports no results establishing simple mappings, stitching, relative-representation transfer, or unpaired alignment.
No recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are measured.
No out-of-distribution evaluation or comparison of a broad range of similarity metrics is reported; the study tests layer, sentence-construction, category-selection, and sign-gauge choices.

The study finds a family-specific component and tests a distillation-lineage explanation, but does not establish shared training data or objectives as the cause, nor compare that explanation with a common model of reality.

rows.subject: 14-model set
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise agreement between per-category truth-axis arrangements, corrected for each model's measured reliability.
rows.value: All 91 pairwise agreements positive; mean 0.798, minimum 0.488, maximum 0.983; exactly one pair fails p < 0.05.
rows.note: Aggregate result across the 91 model pairs; the authors describe the arrangement as shared but not identical.
rows.check: Alignment is incomplete (min 0.488) but high (corrected mean 0.798). V7's 'far from complete' holds only weakly. Values are attenuation-corrected; raw cross-model values are not reported in text. The row says nothing about a scale trend, so it cannot bear on V1.

rows.subject: 14-model set
rows.operation_detail: Compared corrected agreement for models within a family.
rows.note: Within-family agreement exceeds the across-family comparison.
rows.check: A family-specific component exists (0.861 within vs 0.786 across, +0.076, SE 0.020), but it is modest relative to the shared component.

rows.subject: 14-model set
rows.operation_detail: Compared corrected agreement for models from different families.
rows.uncertainty: difference from within-family mean is +0.076 with standard error 0.020
rows.note: Cross-family agreement remains positive, but is lower than within-family agreement.

rows.subject: 14-model set
rows.operation_detail: Measured cross-model arrangement agreement at an early block.
rows.note: The paper reports the early-block agreement as near zero; the peak-minus-early margin has mean +0.554.
rows.check: Lexical-surface control showing the arrangement is built by the blocks. It does not measure how convergence depends on a similarity metric, its settings or the inputs. The text also reports 55 cross-model pairs here versus 91 elsewhere, which is not explained.

rows.subject: 14-model set
rows.operation_detail: Compared per-category axes before any transformer block had computed.
rows.measure: Off-diagonal cosine similarity between per-category axes
rows.value: All 528 off-diagonal cosines are 1.0000; standard deviation is zero.
rows.note: The authors state that category structure does not exist at this layer.
rows.check: Within-model embedding-layer control. All per-category axes are identical, so no cross-model agreement is measured.

rows.subject: 14-model set
rows.operation_detail: Compared the global truth axes fitted with and without a final period in sentence construction.
rows.note: The axes differ substantially across sentence conventions.
rows.check: Within-pipeline comparison of global axes across sentence conventions; not a cross-model convergence measure.

rows.subject: 14-model set
rows.operation_detail: Compared the category arrangement across sentence constructions with and without the final period.
rows.note: The arrangement remains positively related despite the low cosine between the global axes.
rows.check: Within-model arrangement stability across sentence conventions; not cross-model agreement. It shows robustness rather than dependence.

rows.subject: OLMo-2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Compared dictionary reliability with all categories versus categories passing the knowledge gate.
rows.note: The knowledge-gated category selection substantially changes measured reliability.
rows.check: Within-model reliability under category selection. Cross-model agreement on the full category set is not reported, so no dependence of convergence can be read.

rows.subject: 14-model set
rows.operation_detail: Compared within-model dictionary reliability across category-selection protocols.
rows.note: The paper reports lower reliability on the full category set than on the knowledge-restricted set.
rows.check: Same as R8: within-model reliability, not cross-model agreement.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 category bundles
rows.operation_detail: Resampled category dictionaries under six seeds and compared signed arrangements before and after sign repair.
rows.measure: Mantel correlation of signed matrices with the canonical matrix
rows.baseline: Unsigned structure was described as essentially unchanged.
rows.value: Three of six signed matrices were anti-correlated at −0.42, −0.26, and −0.21; after sign repair the correlations were +0.46, +0.59, and +0.73.
rows.note: The authors attribute the instability to thin category-wise sign margins and report that sign repair restores positive agreement.
rows.check: Within-model (Qwen) seed resampling and sign instability; not cross-model convergence.

rows.subject: Cross-family category comparison
rows.operation_detail: Measured cross-family arrangement agreement on the earlier eight-category protocol.
rows.note: This earlier protocol produced a non-significant full cross-family comparison.
rows.check: For V6, cross-family agreement falls to non-significant (+0.233, p=0.15) when P495 is included. The convergence weakens under this category choice, so the state should be observed, not absent. Earlier protocol only (K=8, 888 pairs, no period, no declared gauge).

source_check.locator_found: Section 22, protocol provenance and density diagnostic

rows.subject: Cross-family category comparison
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the earlier cross-family arrangement comparison after excluding category P495.
rows.note: The category subset changes the measured cross-family agreement; the repair diagnostic identifies P495 as a flipped axis.
rows.check: Contrast with R11 (+0.621, p=0.005 excluding P495). Together the two rows show input/category-subset dependence. Earlier protocol only.

rows.subject: Qwen category pool
rows.operation_detail: Compared a pooled global direction with the category axis for P30 (continent).
rows.note: The pooled global direction was captured by the P30 category axis.
rows.check: Within-model diagnostic of the pooled-axis gauge; not cross-model agreement.

rows.subject: OLMo-2-1B
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch without a teacher
rows.operation_detail: Ranked models by mean corrected category-arrangement agreement against all other models.
rows.baseline: Distilled families included Llama-3.2 and Gemma-2.
rows.value: Seventh of fourteen; above Gemma-2-2b and both Llama models.
rows.note: The result does not support shared distillation lineage as a sufficient explanation of the shared arrangement.
rows.check: The state should be judged against V7's cause claim. Shared distillation lineage does not raise agreement: OLMo-2-1B, trained from scratch, ranks 7th (0.804), above the distilled Gemma-2/Llama-3.2 models.

rows.subject: TinyLlama-1.1B
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch without a teacher
rows.operation_detail: Ranked models by mean corrected category-arrangement agreement against all other models.
rows.baseline: Distilled families included Llama-3.2 and Gemma-2.
rows.value: Fifth of fourteen; above Gemma-2-2b and both Llama models.
rows.note: The authors identify this as the cleaner lineage comparison because it shares the Llama architecture with Llama-3.2-1B.
rows.check: Same as R14. TinyLlama ranks 5th (0.817), above Llama-3.2-1B (0.761) at matched architecture.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b-it
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean corrected category-arrangement agreement against other models.
rows.baseline: Agreement with its own base model Gemma-2-2b: 0.882.
rows.value: 0.670; lowest of the fourteen, and the only pair in the campaign failing p < 0.05.
rows.locator: Sections 15 and Limitations and future work
rows.note: The authors report an instruction-tuned outlier, while noting its agreement with its own base model.
rows.check: Instruction tuning displaces Gemma-2-2b-it's arrangement (mean 0.670, lowest of 14), so a training choice affects agreement. This holds in one model only.

source_check.correct: Gemma-2-2b-it has mean corrected agreement 0.670, lowest among fourteen models, and agreement 0.882 with its base. Exactly one of the 91 model pairs fails p < 0.05; this is a pairwise result, not a significance test of Gemma-it's mean. The limitations associate the failing pair with Gemma-it but do not identify its partner.
source_check.locator_found: Section 15; Section 18; Limitations and future work, Gemma-2-2b-it bullet
source_check.problem: The value combines a model-level mean with a pair-level significance result, reproducing ambiguous wording in the limitations.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared the category arrangement with the Qwen2.5-3B base model.
rows.note: The paper contrasts this high base-instruct agreement with the Gemma instruction-tuned outlier.
rows.check: Base-instruct pair sharing pretraining agrees at 0.983; shared training goes with very high agreement.

source_check.locator_found: Limitations and future work, Gemma/Qwen instruction-tuning comparison

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b-it
rows.operation_detail: Compared the category arrangement with the Gemma-2-2b base model.
rows.note: Despite lower agreement with other models, the instruct model agrees with its own base.
rows.check: Gemma base-instruct agreement 0.882 is higher than Gemma-it's agreement with other models.

source_check.locator_found: Limitations and future work, Gemma/Qwen instruction-tuning comparison

relationships.condition: Earlier K=8 protocol (no period, 888 pairs/relation, no declared sign gauge)
relationships.reason: Cross-family agreement goes from +0.621 (p=0.005) to non-significant +0.233 (p=0.15) depending on whether P495 is included (R11, R12). The authors attribute this to a sign-gauge and category-sampling pathology that the final protocol removes.
relationships.display_finding: Under the earlier protocol, cross-family agreement was +0.621 (p=0.005) or +0.233 (p=0.15) depending on category inclusion, an effect the authors attributed to sign conventions and category sampling that the final protocol corrected.

source_check.reason: R11–R12 show significant agreement excluding P495 and non-significant agreement including it. Section 22 identifies sign-orientation and sampling pathology, removed together in the final protocol.

relationships.condition: Final protocol, 14 small LMs, restricted category set
relationships.reason: Agreement is incomplete (min 0.488) but high (corrected mean 0.798, all 91 pairs positive), not 'far from complete' (R1).
relationships.display_finding: All 91 model pairs agreed positively, with corrected mean agreement 0.798 and minimum 0.488.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Final protocol, 14 small LMs, restricted category set
source_check.reason: R1 shows incomplete but high corrected agreement: mean 0.798, minimum 0.488, maximum 0.983. This qualifies V7's characterization of alignment as far from complete in this restricted geometry.

relationships.reason: A measurable family-specific component (0.861 vs 0.786, +0.076, 3.8 SE) is consistent with shared training or architecture contributing to alignment (R2, R3).
relationships.display_finding: Within-family alignment was 0.861 versus 0.786 across families, with a reported difference of +0.076, or 3.8 standard errors.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: R2–R3 establish a family-associated component: 0.861 within families versus 0.786 across families, reported difference +0.076 with SE 0.020. This supports a contribution associated with family, without isolating its causal source.

relationships.condition: Shared distillation lineage as the cause
relationships.reason: Teacher-free OLMo-2-1B and TinyLlama rank 7th and 5th, above both distilled families, so lineage does not explain the agreement (R14, R15).
relationships.display_finding: Teacher-free OLMo-2-1B ranked seventh and TinyLlama fifth, above both distilled families, indicating that shared distillation lineage did not explain agreement.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Shared distillation lineage as the cause
source_check.reason: R14–R15 and Section 24 explicitly report the lineage hypothesis unsupported: teacher-free OLMo-2-1B and TinyLlama rank above the distilled Gemma and Llama models. The challenge is specific to distillation lineage.

relationships.reason: Instruction tuning lowers Gemma-2-2b-it's agreement (0.670) but barely moves Qwen2.5-3B (0.983 with its base). The effect of this training choice is model-dependent (R16, R17, R18).
relationships.display_finding: Instruction tuning reduced Gemma-2-2b-it's agreement to 0.670, whereas Qwen2.5-3B retained 0.983 agreement with its base.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R16–R18 show model-dependent instruction-tuning effects: Gemma-it's mean is 0.670 and base–instruct agreement is 0.882, whereas Qwen base–instruct agreement is 0.983. The training intervention does not have a uniform effect.
